page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 8 physical AMD EPYC 7T83 cores operating at a base frequency of 2.55 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPU accelerators are bundled with this instance type, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench scores, and static web serving throughput fall within the average range. Memory performance shows a significant divergence: cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 1042.55 GB/sec, whereas uncached large-block read and write bandwidths are weak, landing in the bottom 25% at 35.69 GB/sec and 17.06 GB/sec respectively.

Given its high memory density, the ecs.r7a.4xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive applications that do not require massive local storage or high-speed sequential memory writes. It is well-suited for database operations, caching layers like Redis, and small-scale language model inference, where text generation speeds for small models show strong performance. However, workloads requiring heavy uncached memory throughput or local NVMe storage may face performance bottlenecks.
